title: Netanyahu Rival Denounces 'Jewish Terrorism' After Rampage by Israeli Settlers in West Bank
snippet: A series of overnight attacks in the West Bank left cars burned and homes vandalized, prompting top political rival Gadi Eisenkot to condemn the actions as 'Jewish terrorism' while pointing fingers at far-right ministers.
content:
A series of violent overnight rampages across the occupied West Bank has sparked fierce political fallout in Israel, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's primary rival explicitly condemning the attacks as "Jewish terrorism."

Overnight Sunday, groups of Israeli settlers targeted multiple Palestinian villages, including Kufr Malik, Deir as-Sudan, and Deir Abu Masha’al near Ramallah. Attackers set fire to at least a dozen vehicles and sprayed Hebrew graffiti—including the word "revenge"—on civilian homes. While no injuries were immediately reported, Palestinian residents faced widespread property destruction as smoke filled the night air and community warning sirens blared.

Political Fallout and Allegations of Anarchy

The violence drew immediate condemnation from Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief currently attempting to assemble a governing coalition to displace Netanyahu. Eisenkot placed direct blame on far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, accusing them of pushing the region "to the brink of anarchy."

"These are acts of Jewish terrorism, and we must call them by their name," Eisenkot stated, urging Israeli authorities to deploy administrative detentions and targeted counter-terrorism operations against the assailants.

The weekend's incidents follow a separate attack on Thursday, in which a mosque in northern Israel was vandalized and torched. Arab lawmaker Ahmad Tibi slammed the arson, attributing it to toxic political incitement and calling on security forces to act swiftly.

Rising Tension and Lack of Arrests

Prime Minister Netanyahu has not publicly addressed the weekend rampages, continuing a historical pattern of downplaying settler violence as the work of mere "juvenile delinquents." However, Palestinian leaders and international observers warn that such attacks have become systemic.

Yousef Jabareen, leader of the Arab Joint List, stressed that the violence is "the direct result of the deepening occupation," while Palestinian National Initiative president Mustafa Barghouti warned of an escalating crisis threatening civilian safety. According to United Nations estimates, there have been over 410 settler-related attacks linked to the annual olive harvest season since early September.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) condemned the violence, stating that Israeli police are entering the affected Palestinian communities under military escort to gather evidence. As of Sunday evening, law enforcement had announced no arrests in connection with the spates of vandalism and arson.
